sanskrit: yau te mātonmamārja jātāyāḥ pativedanau | durṇāmā tatra mā gṛdhad aliṃśa uta vatsapaḥ ||
english: Those two limb-marks which your mother wiped off you at birth — the pativedanau auspices — let not the Evil-Named one covet them there, neither the aliṃśa nor the vatsapa.

sanskrit: palālānupalālau śarkuṃ kokaṃ malimrucaṃ palījakam | āśleṣaṃ vavrivāsasam ṛkṣagrīvaṃ pramīlinaṃ muṣkayor apa hanmasi ||
english: The palāla, the anupalāla, the śarkuṇa, the koka, the malimruca, the palījaka, the āśleṣa, the vavrivāsasa, the ṛkṣagrīva, the pramīlina — we smite them away from her pudenda.

sanskrit: mā saṃ vṛto mopa sṛpa ūrū māva sṛpo 'ntarā | kṛṇomy asyai bheṣajaṃ bajaṃ durṇāmacātanam ||
english: Let him not press close, let him not creep up against her thighs, let him not glide between them. I prepare for her this remedy, the baja-plant, banisher of the Evil-Named.

sanskrit: durṇāmā ca sunāmā ca- -ubhau saṃvṛtam icchataḥ | arāyam apa hanmasi sunāmā straiṇam icchatām ||
english: Both the Evil-Named and the Fair-Named desire a woman who is enclosed; we smite away the arāya — the Fair-Named desires what belongs to women.

sanskrit: yaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ keśy asura stambajā uta taṇḍikaḥ | arāyān asyā bhaṃsaso muṣkayor apa hanmasi ||
english: He who is dark, hairy, a demon born of the tussock — and the taṇḍika as well — the arāyas from her hind parts and pudenda we drive away.

sanskrit: anujighraṃ pramṛśantaṃ kravyādam uta reriham | arāyaṃ śvakiṣkiṇaṃ bajaḥ piṅgo anīnaśat ||
english: The arāya who sniffs after her and fondles her, the flesh-eater who licks her again and again, the dog-like śvakiṣkiṇa — Baja and Piṅga have utterly destroyed them.

sanskrit: yas tvā suptāṃ tsarati yaś ca dipsati jāgratīm | chāyām iva pra tān sūryaḥ parikrāmam anīnaśat ||
english: He who steals upon you while you sleep, and he who seeks to harm you while you wake — as Sūrya in his circuit destroys shadows, so has he destroyed them all.

sanskrit: yas tvā suptāṃ nipadyate bhrātā bhūtvā piteva ca | bajas tvaṃ sahatām itaḥ klībarūpaṃ tirīṭinam ||
english: He who falls upon you asleep, having taken the form of a brother or like a father — O Baja, you, strike down from here that impotent-shaped tirīṭina.

sanskrit: yaḥ kṛṇoty avatokāṃ mṛtavatsām imāṃ striyam | tam oṣadhe tvaṃ nāśaya- -asyāḥ kamalam añjivam ||
english: He who makes this woman miscarry or causes her calf to be born dead — O herb, destroy him with her kamala and her añjiva.

sanskrit: ye śālāḥ parinṛtyanti sāyaṃ gardabhanādinaḥ kusūlā ye ca kukṣilāḥ kakubhāḥ saramāḥ sumāḥ | tān oṣadhe tvaṃ gandhena viṣūcīnān vi nāśaya ||
english: Those who dance around dwelling-places in the evening, braying like asses — the kusūlas, the kukṣilas, the kakubhas, the saramas, the sumas — O herb, scatter them in all directions with your fragrance and utterly destroy them.

sanskrit: ye kukundhāḥ kukūrabhāḥ kṛttīr dūrśāni bibhrati | klībā iva pranṛtyanto ghoṣāṃ ye kurvate vane tān ito nāśayāmasi ||
english: Those kukundhas and kukūrabhas who wear pelts and unsightly garments, who dance about in the forest like eunuchs and raise a clamour — we drive them away from here.

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ paścāt prapade puraḥ pārṣṇī puro mukham | khalajāḥ śakadhūmajā uruṇḍā ye ca maṭmaṭāḥ kumbhamuṣkā ayāśavaḥ | tān asyā brahmaṇaspate pratībodhena nāśaya ||
english: Those whose toe-tips are behind and whose heels are in front and whose face is in front — the khalajās born of smoke-ash, the uruṇḍas, the maṭmaṭas, the kumbhamuṣkas, the ayāśavas — O Bṛhaspati, destroy them for her with your counter-awakening.

sanskrit: ye sūryaṃ na titikṣanta ātapantam amuṃ divaḥ | arāyān bastavāsino durgandhīṃl lohitāsyān makakān nāśayāmasi ||
english: Those who cannot endure yonder Sūrya blazing in the sky — the arāyas who dwell in he-goats, the foul-smelling, red-mouthed makaka demons — we destroy them.

sanskrit: ye sūryāt parisarpanti snuṣeva śvaśurād adhi | bajaś ca teṣāṃ piṅgaś ca hṛdaye 'dhi ni vidhyatām ||
english: Those who creep away from Sūrya as a daughter-in-law avoids her father-in-law — let both Baja and Piṅga pierce them through the heart.

sanskrit: ya ātmānam atimātram aṃśa ādhāya bibhrati | strīṇāṃ śroṇipratodina indra rakṣāṃsi nāśaya ||
english: Those who carry themselves with excessive self-conceit, placing an undue portion upon themselves, and who prick women in the haunches — O Indra, destroy those rakṣases.

sanskrit: ye pūrve vadhvo yanti haste śṛṅgāṇi bibhrataḥ | āpākesthān prahāsina stambe ye kurvate jyotis tān ito nāśayāmasi ||
english: Those who walk ahead of the bride bearing horns in their hands, the grinning ones who stand at a distance, those who make a light upon a post — we drive them away from here.

sanskrit: paryastākṣāḥ pracaṅkaśā straiṇāḥ santu paṇḍagāḥ | ava bheṣaja pātaya ya imāṃ saṃvivṛtsaty apatiḥ svapatīṃ striyam ||
english: Let them become rolling-eyed, clumsy, effeminate eunuchs — O remedy, strike down the man without a husband who seeks to uncover this woman who has a husband.

sanskrit: uddharṣiṇaṃ munikeśaṃ jambhayantaṃ marīmṛśam | upeṣantam udumbalaṃ tuṇḍenam uta śāluḍam | padā pra vidhya pārṣṇyā sthālīṃ gaur iva syandanā ||
english: The arrogantly excited one, the matted-haired muni-like one, the gnashing one who fondles incessantly, the one who presses close with his udumbala, the tusk-snouted one, and the śāluḍa — pierce them with heel and foot as a cow kicks over the cooking pot.

sanskrit: yas te garbhaṃ pratimṛśāj jātaṃ vā mārayāti te | piṅgas tam ugradhanvā kṛṇotu hṛdayāvidham ||
english: He who tampers with your womb or seeks to kill your child once born — let Piṅga of the fierce bow make him a heart-pierced one.

sanskrit: ye amno jātān mārayanti sūtikā anuśerate | strībhāgān piṅgo gandharvān abhraṃ vāta ivājatu ||
english: Those Gandharvas who lie down beside the lying-in women and kill the newly born — let Piṅga drive those claimants of women's portions away as the wind drives a cloud.

sanskrit: pariśiṣṭaṃ dhārayataṃ yad dhitaṃ māva pādi tat | garbhaṃ ta ugrau rakṣatāṃ bheṣajau nīvibhāryau ||
english: Hold fast what remains of the placenta; let not what was placed there fall away. Let the two fierce remedies, bearers of the girdle-knot, guard your womb.

sanskrit: paripāṇaṃ puruṣāṇāṃ rakṣasām asi cātanam | arāyān sarvān durṇāmno yātudhānān viṣūcīnān vi nāśaya ||
english: You are the all-round protection of men and the expeller of Rakṣases. Scatter in all directions and utterly destroy all arāyas, the Evil-Named, the Yātudhānas.

sanskrit: pavīnasāt taṅgalvāc chāyakād uta nagnakāt | prajāyai patye tvā piṅgaḥ pari pātu kimīdinaḥ ||
english: From the pavīnasa, from the taṅgalva, from the śāyaka, and from the naked one — may Piṅga guard you for offspring and for your husband, keeping away the kimīdina demon.

sanskrit: dvyāsyāś caturakṣāḥ pañcapādād anaṅguleḥ | vṛndād abhi prasarpataḥ pari pāhi varīvṛtāt ||
english: Guard her from the two-mouthed one, from the four-eyed one, from the five-footed one, from the fingerless one — from those who creep forward from a cluster, and from the repeatedly encircling one.

sanskrit: ya āmaṃ māṃsam adanti pauruṣeyaṃ ca ye kravir garbhān khādanti keśavāḥ | arāyān asyā bhaṃsaso muṣkayor apa hanmasi ||
english: Those keśavas who eat raw flesh and the flesh of men, who devour embryos — the arāyas from her hind parts and pudenda we drive away.

sanskrit: piṅga rakṣa jāyamānaṃ pumāṃsaṃ mā striyaṃ kran | āṇḍādo garbhaṃ mā dabhan bādhasvetaḥ kimīdinaḥ ||
english: O Piṅga, guard the one being born; let them not turn the male into a female. Let not the egg-eating ones crush the embryo; drive the kimīdinas away from here.

sanskrit: aprajāstvaṃ mārtavatsam ād rodam agham āvayam | vṛkṣād iva srajaṃ kṛtvā- -apriye prati muñca tat ||
english: Childlessness, the death of offspring, lamentation, evil, misfortune — making them as a garland stripped from a tree, hurl all that upon the enemy woman.

sanskrit: piṅga jahi yātudhānān durgandhīṃl lohitāsyān | tvayā praṇuttāḥ kravyādo viṣvañco yantu nirhatāḥ ||
english: O Piṅga, smite the Yātudhānas, the foul-smelling, the red-mouthed ones. Driven forth by you, let the flesh-eaters go scattered in all directions, utterly slain.
